title: BLACKPINK's Lisa to World Premiere Solo Documentary at Toronto Film Festival
excerpt: Always Lalisa, directed by award-contending filmmaker Sue Kim, will debut as a gala presentation at TIFF 2026 in September, chronicling the K-pop superstar's pivotal year of solo ventures.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Lisa's documentary, Always Lalisa, premieres at TIFF 2026 from September 10-20.
  • The film covers her debut album, Coachella performance, and acting role in The White Lotus.
  • Produced by Sony Music Vision, RCA Records, and Lisa's LLOUD Co.
  • No release date or streaming details announced beyond the TIFF premiere.

BLACKPINK's Lisa — born Lalisa Manobal — will bring her first feature-length solo documentary to one of cinema's most prestigious stages. Always Lalisa has been selected as a gala presentation at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, organizers announced on July 20, placing the K-pop superstar's film alongside titles from directors including Florian Zeller, Chris Rock, and Sian Heder.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=bffWxiIw6Y0

The documentary will world premiere during TIFF's September 10–20 run. A theatrical release date and streaming plans have not yet been disclosed.

What the Documentary Covers

Always Lalisa chronicles a year in which the 29-year-old Thai-born artist stepped away from BLACKPINK's group activities for the first time since childhood. Cameras followed her through the creation and release of her debut solo album Alter Ego, her landmark solo set at Coachella, her acting debut as Mook in HBO's The White Lotus Season 3, and quieter moments including a return to Thailand to spend time with family and longtime friends.

The official synopsis frames the film around the tension between independence and the ticking clock before her return to the group: "LISA confronts the fear and pressure of launching a solo career, pursuing acting, and building a brand, while yearning to maintain a personal life beyond the spotlight."

The Filmmaker Behind the Lens

Director Sue Kim spent an entire year traveling with Lisa to capture the footage. Kim previously directed A24's The Last of the Sea Women, which itself premiered at TIFF in 2024, and served as executive producer on Apple TV+'s K-Pop Idols. Her documentary The Speed Cubers was shortlisted for an Academy Award, establishing her as one of the most sought-after documentary filmmakers working today.

"Following Lisa on this transformative and thrilling year has been a true honor and a cinematic gift," Kim said when the project was first announced by Sony Music Vision in 2025. "There have been so many moments on her journey that I think will surprise people and give a glimpse into her world that no one's ever seen before."

Production and Executive Team

The film is produced by Sony Music Vision in association with RCA Records, Tremolo Productions, Salt Water Productions, and LLOUD Co., Lisa's own label. Morgan Neville and Caitrin Rogers serve as producers for Tremolo Productions, while Sue Kim and Courtney Crockett produce for Salt Water Productions. Executive producers include Alice Kang and Joojong Joe for LLOUD Co., alongside Peter Edge, John Fleckenstein, and Camille Yorrick for RCA Records, and Tom Mackay, Krista Wegener, and Abby Davis for Sony Music Vision.

Lisa's Breakout Solo Year

The documentary lands at a moment when Lisa's solo profile has reached new heights. Alter Ego, released through LLOUD Co. and RCA Records, expanded her audience well beyond BLACKPINK's existing fanbase. Her Coachella performance drew massive viewership, and her turn in The White Lotus earned widespread attention. She is also set to star in Tygo, currently in post-production, marking her feature film acting debut.

BLACKPINK, meanwhile, is reuniting for the "DEADLINE" world tour this summer. The group's members — Lisa, Jisoo, Jennie, and Rosé — had each pursued individual projects during an extended hiatus from group activities.

What to Watch Next

TIFF's full schedule is expected to be announced on August 11. With Always Lalisa positioned as a gala — the festival's highest-profile programming tier — the premiere could serve as a launchpad for a wider awards-season or commercial rollout. For now, fans will be watching for a trailer and details on whether the film heads to theaters, a streaming platform, or both after its Toronto bow.
